verdict.reasoning: Patient states he woke with 'really horrible pain on the left side of my head... a real kind of headache feeling' and that it 'woke me up quite early this morning' around '5:30ish'.
He says, 'I've had a bit of a history with headaches but nothing as severe as this before,' indicating the current headache is new and worse than prior headaches.
He describes prior headaches as 'a bit of a cluster at the front of my head... normally they kind of spread across the front of my head,' implying milder, frontal, more diffuse/bilateral headaches.
He reports 'this time it's just kind of more prominent on the left side' and confirms the headache is 'still present now,' supporting a unilateral, persistent left-sided headache.
In response to bright lights, he says, 'I'm a little bit sensitive. It kind of makes my eyes a little bit sore, but nothing that I can't really handle,' consistent with mild photophobia.
He reports taking paracetamol and when asked if it helped replies, 'Not really, no,' indicating little response.

Regarding lying down: 'it kind of feels a little bit sore at first... but then again, that just kind of soothes a little bit.' When asked if it's ultimately better lying down, he answers, 'Yeah, I would say so.'
He explicitly denies neck stiffness ('No'), fever ('No'), and when asked about nausea says, 'Not really,' indicating no significant nausea.
He states, 'when I first got up this morning my head felt a bit dizzy, but that's kind of... seems to be fine,' describing brief dizziness that resolved.
When asked about thoughts of harming himself, he answers 'No,' indicating denial of self-harm ideation.

He denies prior hypertension ('Have you ever been diagnosed with high blood pressure? Patient: No.') and says he has never had his blood pressure checked ('Have you ever had your blood pressure checked? Patient: No.').

Regarding the headache, he says, 'I've taken some paracetamol' and later, 'Other than Sertraline and having taken paracetamol this morning, nothing else.'
When asked about allergies to medication, he replies, 'Not that I'm aware of, no,' consistent with no known drug allergies.
He reports, 'My mum's had a history of anxiety as well,' indicating maternal anxiety.
When asked if anyone in his family has migraines, he responds, 'No, they haven't,' indicating no family history of migraine.
He adds, 'no kind of like physical illnesses or anything like that' about his parents, indicating no reported physical illnesses in family history.
In response to living situation: 'I live with my partner.'
When asked if he is a smoker, he answers, 'No.'
On exercise: 'So normally I try to go running at least three times a week,' matching running three times per week.
On diet: 'It's okay. It's nothing, nothing really healthy, but it's fine.' This supports that he does not follow a particularly restrictive/special diet.
When asked about pets: 'I have a cat.'

He describes work as 'kind of a bit stressful... a lot of... backlog of work... doing a lot of late nights,' and that this has been 'about a couple of months now,' with mood as 'I get a bit frustrated during the day, but it kind of ebbs and flows,' matching work-related stress with late nights and fluctuating frustration for two months.
The doctor notes, 'obviously I haven't been able to examine you or see you directly,' confirming no physical exam findings due to a remote consult.

Transcript supports: acute severe left-sided headache ('really horrible pain on the left side of my head'), new and worse than prior ('nothing as severe as this before'), possible migraine vs tension ('could be... tension headache... The other possibility is migraine'), mild photophobia ('a little bit sensitive [to bright lights]'), better lying down ('that just kind of soothes... Yeah, I would say so'), and minimal paracetamol effect ('Not really, no').

Doctor links stress/anxiety to headache ('what makes [tension headache] more likely is... you've been under some pressure and you have a history of anxiety') and later suggests addressing work stress, indicating they are considered contributors.

Doctor states, 'the things that we start off first line... would be to start ibuprofen... You can keep on taking paracetamol as well if you like,' advising ibuprofen trial and continuation of paracetamol.
Doctor advises 'a minimum of 1.5 to 2 liters of water or fluids a day, and that's not including coffee or tea,' which excludes caffeinated drinks for hydration.
Doctor recommends 'ensure that you're having a minimum of 7, 8 hours sleep at night, every night,' i.e., sleep hygiene aiming for 7–8 hours.
Doctor suggests work absence: 'maybe consider taking some time off work... maybe having a week off if you self certify that might help with things.'

Doctor says, 'I'd also like you to explore counseling options as well... there's counseling service in your area that I can give you the link for you to self refer,' matching exploration of counseling with self-referral info.

Doctor states, 'I'll also leave a link to some of the danger signs and symptoms of headaches in the notes... what kind of things should trigger you contacting another doctor,' which is safety netting with red-flag information.

Doctor advises, 'If anything changes in the meantime or you get worried or things get worse, feel free... we can reassess the situation,' instructing review if symptoms worsen or concerning features arise.
Doctor plans, 'we'll have a follow up in a week's time' and later, 'we'll touch base in a week's time with me... or one of the other doctors,' confirming a 1-week follow-up.
